themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK, a 387% increase from the 2.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden deterioration in parks and street canopy maintenance that may pose safety and visibility hazards.
evidence: 14 overgrown tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (387% spike, z-score: 8.16)
Spike is statistically significant and marks a clear departure from baseline
Timing aligns with spring season when vegetation growth accelerates
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to understand why maintenance requests have overwhelmed the system this week
Interview residents about blocked sightlines, fallen branches, or hazards they've reported

themes_detail.label: Encampment Growth in Sheepshead Bay
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 8 THIS WEEK, a 611% surge from the 1.1-complaint weekly baseline, indicating a potential homeless crisis or unauthorized settlement problem emerging in the district.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (611% increase, z-score: 6.53)
Represents a dramatic and rapid spike in a typically low-complaint category
Timing suggests a recent influx or visibility event
reporting_angles: Identify locations of encampments and talk to residents and business owners affected
Interview advocates and city officials about services, outreach, and why this area may be experiencing growth now
Document conditions and scale of the problem on the ground

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints skyrocketed to 7 LAST WEEK, a 5500% spike from the 0.1-complaint weekly average, suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, an influx of illegal vendors, or a new complaint awareness campaign.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (5500% spike, z-score: 20.79)
Highest z-score of all spikes, indicating extreme statistical anomaly
Represents a category that is nearly never complained about suddenly appearing at scale
reporting_angles: Determine whether this reflects a new NYPD/DOH enforcement operation targeting illegal street vendors
Interview vendors and business owners about what triggered the complaints
Check if there's been a high-profile vendor incident or policy change in the past 1-2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violation of park rules complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK, a 1100% increase from the 0.2-complaint weekly average, indicating emerging disorder or policy enforcement issues in local parks.
evidence: 3 park rules violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Complements overgrown tree and encampment spikes, suggesting broader park-related problems
Timing is concurrent with other environmental and safety issues
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints and what specific violations are occurring
Talk to Parks Department about staffing and enforcement capacity during spring season

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% jump from the 0.2-complaint weekly average, suggesting either building maintenance failures or a cluster of mechanical breakdowns in residential buildings.
evidence: 4 elevator complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Represents a rare and sudden spike in a typically non-complaint category
Timing is slightly older than other current spikes but still recent
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings filed complaints and investigate ownership/maintenance records
Interview residents about wait times and impacts on disabled and elderly tenants
